text:
carmen: Hey support — since ~yesterday our production webapp started seeing intermittent 429s. We use one API key per project but the 429 responses include X-RateLimit-Scope: org:acct-12345. Nothing changed in our code; any ideas?

olivia: sorry for the trouble — can you paste one of the 429 response headers (X-Request-ID + X-RateLimit-* lines) and confirm whether traffic goes through your NAT/proxy or directly to Redwood? Also: are you using API keys or OAuth?

carmen: sample response (masked):
```
HTTP/2 429 Too Many Requests
date: Tue, 24 Nov 2025 18:34:12 GMT
x-request-id: rq_ABC123456
x-rate-limit-limit: 100000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 169? <-- our client saw 0
x-rate-limit-scope: org:acct-12345
content-type: application/json
```
Traffic goes through our internal proxy (egress NAT) and we use API keys (sk- tokens).

olivia: thanks. scope shows org-level quota being hit. Two quick possibilities: 1) requests are being attributed to org (rather than api_key) because the key was unrecognized at attribution time, or 2) your org quota actually saturated from another project/burst. Did you recently migrate billing or enable consolidated-org billing?

carmen: we did a billing consolidation last week (moved two projects under the same org). We also had a batch job that restarted on a node pool yesterday and it retried a job a few hundred times due to transient 502s. Could that consume org quota across projects?

ashok: oncall-sre here — I pulled rq_ABC123456 from the logs. The request reached our edge from nat-1 (35.202.x.x). Our attribution order is: api_key -> project -> org -> ip. If the presented API key is not found/valid at attribution, we fall back to org or IP. Can you confirm the exact Authorization header string (mask the key) or the key fingerprint?

carmen: our deploy pipeline rotates keys; one of the older workers might have an out-of-date key. Header looked like: `Authorization: Bearer sk-old-XXXX****` (we masked the middle). We think some replicas used the old token during the restart window.

ashok: that matches a common pattern — revoked/unknown key => system attributes to org (or IP) and then org quota gets drained by runaway retries. Please run this from an affected host and paste the headers (mask key body):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-key-masked>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/models/list
```
We just need the response headers, not the body. Also grab the X-Request-ID from a 429 sample.

carmen: running now — returned 429 with same scope. here's the 429 header we grabbed: `x-request-id: rq_ABC123456` and `x-rate-limit-scope: org:acct-12345`. Our app logs show the failing worker used `sk-old-...` during the restart window.

olivia: OK. We're going to do two things immediately: 1) temporary emergency exception for your webapp key so it doesn't get blocked by the org quota while you finish rotation, 2) escalate to billing to review org consumption and check for runaway batch. I'll create a short-lived override for api_key:sk-new-******* (we need the fingerprint, not the raw key).

marcel: billing here — I can see a spike from project "batch-worker" starting 2025-11-24T17:20Z with lots of retries. We can grant a one-time quota bump or apply credits, but we prefer to fix the root cause (retry backoff). If you want a temporary increase, tell us which project or key to exempt and for how long.

carmen: please exempt the production webapp key (sk-new-****) for 1 hour. We'll rotate and redeploy the workers with the new key and patched retry logic (exponential backoff + jitter).

ashok: done — I've applied a 1h api_key override tied to the key fingerprint (fingerprint: fp_7a9f...). After the override took effect I see X-RateLimit-* for that key reflecting per-key quota (not org). Can you verify traffic is healthy now?

carmen: traffic looks normal now, 200s returning, thank you :relieved: We'll push the key rotation in the next 10m and update you with request-ids for verification.

olivia: next steps summarized:
- carmen: rotate keys across all replicas and redeploy; add ephemeral check to fail-safe if old key is present.
- carmen/devs: patch retry loop in batch job to avoid tight spins (exponential backoff + jitter).
- marcel (billing): confirm final org quota reallocation or offer credits if needed.
- ashok (SRE): remove emergency override after validation window.

ashok: FYI for internal notes: this is a typical attribution edge-case where revoked/unknown api key -> attribution falls back to org and can surface as unexpected org-level 429s. Consider adding improved logging at attribution stage to emit key fingerprint (masked) + resolution reason (missing/unrecognized/revoked) to make future triage easier.

carmen: noted, thanks everyone. I'll post back once rotation completes with one or two request ids to close the ticket. :thumbsup:
